title: ₹980 dispute, ₹2.51 crore frozen
summary: A ₹980 UPI spend by a mule froze a liquor merchant's entire ₹2.51 crore balance; LienLine liens ₹980 and releases the rest.

complaint.narrative: I got a call at 10:50 am on 14 Sep from a man saying my bank KYC had expired and the account would be blocked. He sent a link and I entered my details. At 11:02 Rs 98,000 was debited by IMPS to account XXXX9834 at Sahyadri Bank, UTR 626152099011. I called 1930 at 1:10 pm.

grievances.text: Our entire current account of ₹2.51 crore is frozen over a ₹980 counter sale. We cannot pay excise duty, salaries or the distillery. We ask that only the disputed amount be held.

reasons.text: The victim's money arrived via T1 (₹98,000.00 of ₹98,000.00 from A1). The balance fell to ₹2,370.00 after T9, which caps what can still be traced: ₹2,370.00 under LIBR (lowest intermediate balance).

Full freeze justified by 4 mule signals: On the I4C suspect registry; Account opened 41 days ago; 98% of available funds passed straight through; Half of T1 moved on within 29 minutes. The amount traceable from this complaint alone is ₹2,370.00 under LIBR; the whole balance is held because of these signals, not this complaint's amount.

Other tracing rules give FIFO ₹2,370.00, LIFO ₹2,020.00, PRO_RATA ₹2,361.57. LIBR is used because it is the accepted standard for mixed funds: it never counts the holder's later, clean credits as the victim's money.
₹980.00 of the victim's money is identifiable here under LIBR: it arrived via T9 (₹980.00 of ₹980.00 from A2), and the balance never fell below it afterwards.

The current hold of ₹2,51,00,000.00 covers the whole balance. MP High Court, Archana v State of MP, 27 Jul 2026 and Rajasthan High Court, Shree Balaji Enterprises v RBI, 20 Aug 2026 limit a hold to the identifiable disputed amount, so ₹2,50,99,020.00 is released.

Other tracing rules give FIFO ₹980.00, LIFO ₹980.00, PRO_RATA ₹965.36. LIBR is used because it is the accepted standard for mixed funds: it never counts the holder's later, clean credits as the victim's money.
The victim's money arrived via T2 (₹44,650.00 of ₹45,000.00 from A2). The balance fell to ₹1,200.00 after T8, which caps what can still be traced: ₹1,200.00 under LIBR (lowest intermediate balance).
Mule signals present (Account opened 120 days ago; 97% of available funds passed straight through), but no registry hit and fewer than 3 linked complaints, so a full freeze is not justified.

Other tracing rules give FIFO ₹1,190.67, LIFO ₹0.00, PRO_RATA ₹1,164.68. LIBR is used because it is the accepted standard for mixed funds: it never counts the holder's later, clean credits as the victim's money.

letters.subject: Justification for Full Balance Freeze on Account XXXX9834 following Cyber-Fraud Complaint
letters.body:
This letter serves to justify the decision to maintain a full freeze on the balance of Account XXXX9834, held by Vikas Kumar, Sahyadri Bank. This action is taken in response to the NCRP acknowledgement 31509260012345 and the notice under Section 106 BNSS dated 16 Sep 2026 from SI R. Verma, Cyber PS, Bhopal.

The current hold is set at ₹2,370.00, which represents the entire balance. The decision to keep this full freeze is based on significant mule signals, including the account being opened only 41 days ago, 98% of available funds passing straight through, and half of T1 moving within 29 minutes. Furthermore, the account is flagged on the I4C suspect registry.

While a hold is typically limited to the identifiable disputed amount, as per MP High Court, Archana v State of MP, 27 Jul 2026, and Rajasthan High Court, Shree Balaji Enterprises v RBI, 20 Aug 2026, the traceable amount to this complaint alone under LIBR is ₹2,370.00. Given the high risk indicators, the full freeze of ₹2,370.00 is necessary for investigation.

Nodal Officer, Sahyadri Bank

letters.subject: Instruction to Replace Whole-Account Freeze with Lien on Account XXXX6876
letters.body:
This letter serves as a formal instruction regarding the hold placed on Account XXXX6876, held by Narmada Wines & Spirits, Sahyadri Bank.

We acknowledge the current hold amount of ₹2,51,00,000.00, which covers the whole balance, pursuant to NCRP acknowledgement 31509260012345 and the notice under Section 106 BNSS dated 16 Sep 2026 from SI R. Verma, Cyber PS, Bhopal.

Based on the legal precedents set by MP High Court, Archana v State of MP, 27 Jul 2026, and Rajasthan High Court, Shree Balaji Enterprises v RBI, 20 Aug 2026, a hold must be limited to the identifiable disputed amount. Therefore, we instruct you to replace the whole-account freeze with a lien of only ₹980.00, which is traceable to the complaint under LIBR, corresponding to the credit received via UTR 626843483256.

Please release the remaining amount of ₹2,50,99,020.00 from the hold immediately.

Nodal Officer, Sahyadri Bank

letters.subject: Reply to Grievance Regarding Hold on Account XXXX6876
letters.body:
This is in reference to the grievance received on 22 Sep 2026 concerning the hold placed on your account, XXXX6876, held with Sahyadri Bank.

We acknowledge the NCRP acknowledgement 31509260012345 and the notice under Section 106 BNSS dated 16 Sep 2026 from SI R. Verma, Cyber PS, Bhopal. The current hold amount is ₹2,51,00,000.00.

Based on the legal precedents set by the MP High Court, Archana v State of MP, 27 Jul 2026, and the Rajasthan High Court, Shree Balaji Enterprises v RBI, 20 Aug 2026, the hold is limited to the identifiable disputed amount. We have determined that a lien of ₹980.00 is applicable, as this amount is traceable under the lowest intermediate balance rule, corresponding to the credit via UTR 626843483256.

Consequently, we are releasing ₹2,50,99,020.00 from the hold. The remaining lien of ₹980.00 will remain in place.

Nodal Officer, Sahyadri Bank
